messages.text: he never does anything right. i'm so tired of carrying everything.

It sounds like you are carrying an incredibly heavy load, and that exhaustion is completely understandable. Feeling unsupported when you are doing so much can be deeply frustrating. I am here to listen without judgment as you process these feelings. Can you tell me more about what specifically feels the heaviest right now?
if i don't keep on him, we'll end up broke, he'll lose his job, the kids will see him as a failure. i'm the only one making sure things don't go completely off the rails

It sounds like you are carrying a deep fear for your family's stability and future. Shouldering that entire burden by yourself must feel incredibly isolating and exhausting. Have you reached a point where you no longer trust him to handle his own responsibilities? How would you feel about exploring ways to step back from this constant vigilance?
he makes me feel like i have to. he doesn't take anything seriously. i tell him every day — this isn't how things were in my family. we had standards.

It sounds like you are trying to protect your family by upholding the standards you grew up with. Repeating these expectations daily without change must feel very discouraging. Those past experiences clearly shape how you view safety and responsibility today. I wonder if holding onto those expectations is adding to your exhaustion rather than solving the problem?
i just want someone to tell me it's not wrong to want him to do better. is that too much to ask?

No, it is not too much to ask for a partner to contribute meaningfully to the family. Your desire for reliability and shared responsibility is a completely reasonable expectation. It is understandable that you feel exhausted when you are the only one holding things together. How does it feel to hear that your expectations are valid?
is it really so bad to talk tough to him if it's the only thing that makes him move? i'm not being cruel — i'm trying to help him be better.

Your intention to help him succeed is clear and comes from a place of caring. It is understandable to feel stuck when tough talk seems like the only thing that works. Sometimes, however, pressure can create resistance rather than cooperation over time. How do you think he responds when you aren't in that tough mode?
he doesn't respond at all when i'm nice. it's like he doesn't even hear me. i have to be sharp just to get a reaction.

It is incredibly frustrating to feel unheard when you are trying to connect gently. It makes sense that you view this sharpness as protection rather than cruelty. That cycle of needing to be sharp to get a reaction can be very exhausting. How does using that approach impact your own peace of mind?
i'm just so tired. i can't keep being the bad cop all the time. but if i don't, who will make sure he doesn't mess up?

It is completely understandable that you are exhausted from playing the enforcer. The fear that things will fall apart without you is a heavy weight to carry. His mistakes are ultimately his own to learn from, even if that is hard to watch. How would you feel if you allowed him to experience some of those results without your intervention?
if he slips up at work, he could lose his job. and if he loses his job, they might take away his status. i'm not even exaggerating — i've seen it happen. one mistake and he's out.

It sounds like the stakes feel incredibly high, and your fear is rooted in real observations you have made. It makes sense that you feel responsible for preventing such a devastating outcome. Living in that state of high alert must be exhausting for your nervous system. How does this constant worry affect your ability to rest?
sometimes i tell him he's lucky i stayed. that no one else would put up with him — not here, not with his background. i say it to wake him up.

It sounds like you feel these words are the only way to get through to him. While your intention is to wake him up, comments on his worth can sometimes deepen shame rather than spark change. I wonder how saying those things affects your own peace of mind. Have you considered what might happen if you tried expressing your fear without attacking his character?
it's not an attack. it's the truth. he does need to hear it. if i don't say it, who will?

It sounds like you feel responsible for his survival in a very high-stakes environment. You are convinced that your hard truths are the only thing keeping him safe. I wonder how he experiences these conversations when he is feeling vulnerable. How do you think he responds when he feels safe enough to be imperfect?
you don't get it. i'm not tearing him down — i'm holding him up. if i stop, he'll fall. simple as that.

I hear that you feel I am not seeing the full picture. You see yourself as the only thing keeping him from falling. That is a tremendous burden to carry alone. How does that belief affect your ability to rest?
i can't sleep. i lie there thinking about all the ways he could mess up. i'm so tired. but if i don't watch everything, who will?

It sounds like your mind cannot rest because you feel solely responsible for preventing disaster. That constant state of alert is taking a heavy toll on your body and spirit. You are right that you are tired, but this level of control might be costing you your own peace. How would you feel if you allowed yourself to rest, even if he is not perfect?
